headline: Grain holds steady overnight ahead of export sales report
lead: Corn is trading at $4.80 overnight, barely off Wednesday's $4.80¾ settle. Beans sit at $12.73¼, down 4 cents, with weekly export sales due Thursday at 7:30 a.m. CT. Nothing has moved yet, so the board is sitting right where harvest left it.
teaser: Corn and beans sit near flat overnight with export sales due at 7:30 a.m. CT.

one_number.unit: soybean meal's spot in its 52-week range
one_number.context: Meal is near a 52-week high while soybeans themselves sit well below theirs, a sign the crush margin is carrying the soy complex, not bean demand.

sections.title: Corn and beans wait on export sales
sections.body:
- Corn is at **$4.80**, down three quarters of a cent from Wednesday's $4.80¾ settle.
- Beans are at $12.73¼, down 4 cents, with soybean meal up 1.0% to $368.30 while soybean oil fell 0.9% to $66.47.
- Weekly export sales print Thursday at 7:30 a.m. CT, and nothing in the numbers above reflects it yet.
sections.so_what: Meal keeps pulling the soy complex while the raw bean price goes nowhere.

sections.title: Cattle and hogs ease back slightly
sections.body:
- Live cattle are at $223.90, down 0.3% from Wednesday's $224.62 settle, and feeders are at $340.95, down 0.6%.
- Hogs are nearly flat at $75.55, just below Wednesday's $75.60.
- No report or news explains the pullback, it looks like normal give-back after weeks of gains.
sections.so_what: Small give-back after a long climb, nothing more.

sections.title: Crude slips as Trump weighs easing tanker sanctions
sections.body:
- WTI crude is at $93.80 overnight, down 1.4% from Wednesday's $95.09 settle.
- The pullback follows word that the administration may ease sanctions on tankers moving Russian, Iranian and Venezuelan oil, adding supply to a tight tanker market.
sections.so_what: Crude easing hasn't reached diesel yet, and diesel is what farmers actually buy.

outside_the_pit.title: Judge blocks USDA reorganization and office closures
outside_the_pit.body: A federal judge ruled USDA's reorganization plan likely violates a congressional directive and ordered a halt to staff moves and office closures.

watch_list.desc: Export sales report. Soybean sales under 1.5 MMT would look soft against the current price.
Diesel above $6 even as crude eases below $94 would widen the input-cost gap further.
Corn back under $4.78 would say harvest supply is starting to weigh on the board.

source_summary: CME/CBOT overnight quotes, USDA, oilprice.com, feedstuffs.com, beefmagazine.com, thefencepost.com, farmpolicynews.illinois.edu

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.93 vs $4.62 projected (+6.7%), 10 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.87 vs $11.09 projected (+16.1%), 10 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 14, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.95. RMA posts soybeans at $12.88. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 14. Oct 1-31 window, most states.
